blocks.text: The Digital Experience (ZDX) service is built as a multi-tenant, cloud-based monitoring platform to probe, benchmark, and measure the digital experiences for every single user within your organization.

ZDX relies on the Zscaler Client Connector to perform synthetic probing to a desired Software as a Service (SaaS) application or internet-based service (e.g., OneDrive, Gmail, etc.). Zscaler Client Connector is the unified client that supports our Internet & SaaS and Private Access services today. ZDX support is natively integrated within Zscaler Client Connector, and runs as a standalone lightweight module that is upgraded independently of the Zscaler Client Connector core process.
To configure Zscaler Client Connector for your organization, see What Is Zscaler Client Connector?, Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for ZDX, and Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.
ZDX lets you monitor granular details for users, devices, applications, and more in your org. With ZDX, you can:

blocks.item: Proactively monitor every user device in your organization to detect user experience and productivity issues.
Grade your digital experience by referencing the ZDX Score over time for your organization and each application, location, department, and user.
Triage performance issues and pinpoint whether the issue is in the local network, a user's device, the ISP provider, or within the Zscaler cloud.
Use Zscaler’s unified client, Zscaler Client Connector, to implement ZDX on Windows, macOS, Android, Android on ChromeOS, and iOS devices.

Monitor general data center information and your key SaaS applications (i.e., Outlook Online, Salesforce, Box, etc.) using HTTP, ICMP, or UDP synthetic probes running on user devices in near real time.
Collect real-time device health information (i.e., CPU usage, memory usage, Network IO, Disk IO, Wi-Fi signal strength, etc.) for your user devices.
Hop-by-Hop network path visualization from the client device to the destination device.

Remote troubleshooting capabilities to perform detailed analyses of problematic devices (i.e., system process-level monitoring, full network path information including the Autonomous System Number (ASN), ISP information, country hop information, and packet tracing).
Executive insights reports and digital experience analytics aggregated at organization, location, and application levels.
